source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyaya 18: Kadru asks Vinata the colour of Uchchaihshravas; Vinata says white, Kadru that the tail is black; they wager slavery and agree to look the next day; Kadru orders her thousand sons to become black hairs in the tail; those who refuse she curses to burn in Janamejaya's snake sacrifice; Brahma, seeing the serpents grown many and venomous, lets the curse stand and gives Kashyapa the knowledge that cures poison.
structure: From episode 11: COLD OPEN (the hook over the episode's strongest image, big on-screen text from frame 1; KIT.series.hookCard) → title (the hook's post) → RECAP (≈2.5 s) → STORY (with a brief cut to Sauti at the Naimisha fire) → the cliffhanger image + line → a silent ≈1.5 s Next card that dissolves back into the first frame (KIT.series.loopNextScene).

strings.stakeLabel: The loser becomes the winner's slave

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: What if a bet about a horse's tail could cost you your freedom?
lines.say: What if a bet about a horse's tail [p:80] could cost you your freedom?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (moving from frame 1): close on the white horse's tail streaming in the sunset wind; dark strands creep into it, one by one; behind, two women's silhouettes face each other. The question in big text from frame 1.

lines.text: The white horse had risen from the churning of the ocean.
lines.say: The white horse had risen from the churning of the ocean.
lines.note: RECAP: episode 16's closing image as a memory: Sauti's medallion of the white horse on the shore.

lines.speaker: vinata
lines.note: STORY 1 (Vinata speaks): the shore at sunset (NEW LIGHT: low gold from the right). Vinata, LARGE, calm, looking out at the horse.

lines.speaker: kadru
lines.note: STORY 2 (Kadru speaks): reverse angle: Kadru, LARGE, the green glint in her eye, a thin smile; she points at the tail.

lines.text: The loser would be the winner's slave. They would look at dawn.
lines.say: The loser would be the winner's slave. [p:200] They would look at dawn.
lines.note: STORY 3: the two sisters face to face, the setting sun between them; a card: 'The loser becomes the winner's slave'; the sun goes down (beats[2] 'dawn': the sky darkens to night).

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: But Kadru did not wait for dawn.
lines.say: But Kadru did not wait for dawn.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti at the Naimisha fire, the sages leaning in, a sixth angle: over the elder's shoulder): a sly beat.

lines.speaker: kadru
lines.text: "My sons, hang from his tail, like black hairs."
lines.say: My sons, [p:150] hang from his tail, [p:100] like black hairs.
lines.note: STORY 4 · NEW PLACE AND LIGHT: the serpents' grove at night, deep green moonlight among great roots. Kadru, her five-hooded diadem glinting, speaks to her sons rearing round her (many hoods, varied).
STORY 5 · THE TURN (≈ 50 %): after a 350 ms rest: a row of serpents turn their hoods away from her, one by one (beats[0]).

lines.speaker: kadru
lines.text: "Then burn in the fire of Janamejaya's snake sacrifice!"
lines.say: Then burn [p:100] in the fire [p:80] of Janamejaya's snake sacrifice!
lines.note: STORY 6 (Kadru's curse): Kadru's finger high (curse pose), her eye green fire; above, a gold-ringed medallion opens on the snake sacrifice of episode 8, serpents falling into the flames (a callback). beats = 'burn', 'fire', 'Janamejaya's'.

lines.text: Brahma let the curse stand: the serpents had grown too many, and too venomous.
lines.say: Brahma let the curse stand: [p:150] the serpents had grown too many, [p:80] and too venomous.
lines.note: STORY 7: Brahma on his lotus on Meru's summit, grave, his hand lowered (beats[1]); the serpents' shadows multiply below (beats[2]).

lines.text: And to Kashyapa he gave the knowledge that cures all poison.
lines.say: And to Kashyapa [p:100] he gave the knowledge that cures all poison.
lines.note: STORY 8: Kashyapa, seated, receives a small light from Brahma's raised hand into his cupped palms (beats[1]); name card.

lines.text: At dawn the sisters flew out over the ocean to look.
lines.say: At dawn [p:100] the sisters flew out over the ocean to look.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger image): dawn over the endless ocean; the two sisters flying out over it, small against the sky, toward the horizon.
The short, silent Next card: a glimpse of episode 18: the horse's tail, streaked with black; then the loop back to frame 1.
